reserveReview.rationale: Re-opened 2026-08-29. Nest's positions API reports settled holdings of $73,341,323.55 in LiquidStone II/OALS2T, $2,277,342.34 in nTBILL, $448,715.37 in USDC, $287,140.97 in USDT/USDT0, and $45,317.59 in pUSD. The NAV endpoint reports $77,580,402.06; the $1,180,562.25 difference is carried as an explicit NAV reconciliation residual rather than allocated to an invented asset. The positions payload also contains a $1.2m pending OALS2T withdrawal; the production nest-vault-positions adapter intentionally rejects positive pending withdrawals, so this current snapshot cannot be treated as a successful live-reserve observation. nBASIS is zero. Percentages are normalized to NAV and retain the fund-level private-credit unknown. Re-opened again 2026-09-01 against the current production live-reserve capture: the nest-vault-positions adapter emits the private-credit position under the exact name "Nest private and structured credit vaults", so the reviewed row's trailing "(LiquidStone II / OALS2T)" qualifier prevented it from joining the live exposure and left the largest slice unclassified. The qualifier was moved out of the row name; the LiquidStone II / OALS2T identification is unchanged and carried by issuerOrObligor and this rationale. Weights remain the 2026-08-29 reading and are not identity for the join. The private-credit row's liquidityHorizon was also corrected from seven-days to over-seven-days, because the join repair is what first makes that field score and the previously curated value had no source behind it: Nest's liquidity and redemptions page (re-opened 2026-09-01) states the maximum settlement window for most strategies is T+2 to T+5 but that strategies holding longer-duration real-world assets run 30 to 90 days, LiquidStone II is a Brazilian FIDC receivables sub-fund in that longer-duration class, the positions payload carries a pending OALS2T withdrawal rather than a settled one, and the two sibling Nest vault entries (inalpha-nest, nwisdom-nest) already classify the identically named live exposure as over-seven-days. The same 2026-08-29 positions payload also reports pending-deposit transactions; the adapter's exact "Nest pending deposits" row is classified as an explicit Nest vault queue exposure, without asserting an underlying asset class or adding unsupported liquidity terms.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Nest positions and NAV APIs fetched 2026-08-29, normalized to reported nOPAL NAV; settled positions plus explicit reconciliation residual
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: LiquidStone II's obligor-level receivable composition, the $1,180,562.25 NAV residual, the pending OALS2T withdrawal state, fund service providers, and any fund-level financial audit are not public. Stablecoin and nTBILL legs are identified. nBASIS has zero balance.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Nest documents that underlying-asset cash and securities sit with third-party custodians rather than Nest itself, and BlackOpal describes LiquidStone II as a single-investor sub-fund of a Brazilian FIDC holding receivables acquired via true sale, which supports segregated, bankruptcy-remote treatment. The FIDC's custodian, administrator, and obligor-level positions are not named publicly, no fund-level financial attestation exists, and rehypothecation terms are not published.
